purpose: Quality reference for upgrading the 850-word database. These entries demonstrate the English-thinking structure; they are not yet the complete S80 list.

items.core_image: A bridge / connector that places the subject at an identity, location, or state.
items.core_logic: BE does not launch an action; it connects the subject to what situation it is in.
meaning_growth: foundation for be + doing and be + done

confusions.difference: Action verbs encode the action itself; BE locates/connects the subject to a state or information.

items.card_metaphor: A 3D bridge connecting the subject to three destinations: identity, location and state.

items.core_image: A finger or arrow precisely targeting a point.
items.core_logic: AT compresses a target into a point and directs attention/action toward that point.
meaning_growth: target of an action or attention

confusions.difference: AT conceptualizes a point; ON a surface/contact relation; IN a containing region.

items.card_metaphor: A bright target point with an arrow/finger locking onto it.

items.core_image: Two surfaces in contact / something attached to a surface or connection.
items.core_logic: ON builds a contact or connected relation that can extend from physical surfaces to active connections and attached states.

confusions.difference: ON suggests contact/connection; OFF suggests detachment/disconnection.

items.card_metaphor: Two clean 3D surfaces snapping into contact, with a connected/active branch.

items.core_image: An object enclosed by a three-dimensional container or surrounding state.
items.core_logic: IN conceptualizes something as being within the bounds of a containing region, physical or abstract.

confusions.difference: IN gives the target volume/boundaries; ON gives surface contact; AT reduces it to a point.

items.card_metaphor: A transparent 3D container enclosing an object; branches show room, time and emotion containers.

items.core_image: An arrow oriented toward a destination or goal.
items.core_logic: TO encodes target-directed orientation: something is pointed, transferred or conceptually directed toward a goal.

confusions.difference: TO highlights direction/target rather than simply where something already is.

items.card_metaphor: A luminous 3D arrow traveling from origin to a clearly marked target.

items.core_image: Visual information arrives in the eyes/awareness.
items.core_logic: SEE is primarily reception/perception: the image enters awareness without emphasizing deliberate eye movement.

confusions.difference: LOOK is the deliberate turning/directing of the eyes.
WATCH keeps attention on something through time/change.

items.card_metaphor: An object enters a visual field and reaches an eye/awareness node.

items.core_image: The eyes deliberately turn toward a target.
items.core_logic: LOOK is an intentional eye-direction action; another word such as AT often supplies the target.

confusions.difference: SEE receives visual information; LOOK directs the eyes.
WATCH adds sustained attention over a changing process.

items.card_metaphor: A pair of eyes rotates, then a beam points to a target dot.

items.core_image: The eyes stay with a target as it changes over time.
items.core_logic: WATCH means sustained visual attention to a process, movement, or changing scene.

confusions.difference: LOOK directs the eyes; WATCH keeps them engaged over time.

items.card_metaphor: A moving object leaves a short time trail while the eye tracks it continuously.
